text:
carmen_sales: quick question from an inbound POC — large EU fintech wants 'EU-only' for first 6 months, then gradually open to APAC. they prefer not to buy Dedicated right now. can we pin their tenant to EU and then switch routing later without data egress to other regions?
ajay_se: short answer: yes with caveats. we support tenant-level region affinity (soft pin) in Hosted, but hard guarantees (no cross-region egress at all) require Dedicated or Private.
lena_ops: details: Hosted can honor a region preference header and prefer eu nodes, but fallback paths exist for failover. that means metadata/replication might cross regions for HA. if customer needs cryptographic residency (no keys outside EU), need Private + BYOK.
sam_infra: implementation note — for Hosted we map tenant -> preferred_region in routing table. example request header for preference:```
POST /v1/generate
Host: api.redwood.ai
Authorization: Bearer ${TOKEN}
x-tenant-id: fin-xyz
x-region-hint: eu-west-1
```
This will prefer eu capacity but not guarantee zero-ejection.
carmen_sales: ok, customer asked about cost delta vs Dedicated — can you give a quick order-of-magnitude? they want to justify to procurement.
lena_ops: rough: Hosted with region affinity is normal usage pricing (pay-per-token). if they later need Dedicated for strict residency, expect 3-5x base hosted unit cost depending on commit and model size (GPUs). timeline for Dedicated provisioning usually 4-8 weeks.
ajay_se: also call out feature cost: enabling tenant pinning + stricter SLAs may need a reserved pool (we can scope as a lighter 'regional reservation' cheaper than full Dedicated but still a monthly minimum).
emma_legal: from compliance POV — what we can promise in Hosted: contractual clause for 'preferred region processing' and breach notifications. we cannot sign 'no data leaves EU' unless it's Private/Dedicated with on-prem or VPC egress controls. need to flag in security questionnaire.
carmen_sales: prospect also asks about sub-processors and KMS — will customer keys ever be outside EU?
sam_infra: we use cloud KMS per-region for encrypted secrets. Hosted currently uses multi-region-managed keys; for EU-only key residency you need Private with BYOK/HSM or a Dedicated setup integrated with a regional KMS.
lena_ops: sub-processor list: current third-parties in EU: cloud-provider-eu, observability-eu, logging-archive (EU region replicas). APAC infra exists but won't be used if tenant stays pinned — except for DR scenarios. I'll attach official sub-processor doc in the follow-up.
carmen_sales: timeline question: customer wants a POC in two weeks with EU-only traffic flow validation (no cross-region calls except for auth). doable?
ajay_se: two-week POC: possible to run a scoped test by routing a test tenant to EU capacity only and monitoring egress, but we'd need approval from infra for a hard policy toggle (disable fallbacks) and legal for scoped SLA exceptions. ops + infra involvement required.
lena_ops: i can spin up a temporary regional policy for a test tenant (no fallback to APAC) for 14 days, but it's manual and requires a support ticket and on-call review. we'll document the scope and revoke after POC.
emma_legal: I'll draft a narrow scoping statement for the customer that limits guarantees to the POC window and lists residual risks.
deploy-bot: scheduled task created — ticket #RD-POC-482 in ops with owners @lena_ops and @sam_infra, target start in 3 business days.
carmen_sales: perfect. last question: any recommended language for the customer's security questionnaire where they ask "How do you ensure region-only processing?"
ajay_se: recommended phrasing: "Redwood Inference supports tenant-level region affinity in Hosted. For strict cryptographic and contractual residency guarantees, Dedicated or Private deployments are required. For POCs, Redwood can enable scoped regional policies for a limited period to validate traffic flows."
lena_ops: i'll follow up with a 1-page checklist: required approvals, expected monitoring signals (netflow, KMS region audit, token latency), and a step-by-step to enable the temporary policy.
carmen_sales: thanks team — i'll update the customer and paste their questionnaire back here once they send it. :thumbsup:
